Requirements for handler pairs in detail
This section shows why careful work counts

Handler Pair Standards

This section sets the basics for safe, steady service at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. The goal is to keep every animal calm, every handoff clear, and every record clean.

Handlers work in pairs when loading, moving, or checking a pet, and they keep voices low and steps smooth. One handler watches the animal, while the other handles paperwork, gear, and door control. If a pet shows stress, the pair slows down and uses the calmest humane method available. The senior coordinator reviews any rough case and decides whether service can continue or needs a higher level of review.

For small dog requests, <<FACT F074>>. Staff then confirm the booking file and make sure the crate, labels, and owner notes match. For large dog travel, <<FACT F081>>. If a fee is due, <<FACT F057>>. No handler may guess, waive, or rewrite a charge on their own.

When a traveler brings a pet, the desk checks the fit of the plan, the condition of the carrier, and the readiness of the handler pair. Felix Mori and Isaac Costa may be used as sample traveler names in training notes, but service decisions must still follow the file. Murphy, if listed, gets the same calm treatment as any other pet.

If anything is unclear, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
